profile.reading: This is Noovle DC Rivoli, one of several Noovle branded data centers around Turin, Italy, at Via Ferrero 10 in Rivoli, west of the city center. An engineering case study by Italian firm Open Building, working with mechanical and electrical designer Deerns Italia on a project referred to internally as The Rooster, documents a 2021 through 2022 conversion of an industrial warehouse into a new data center for Noovle S.p.A. on a roughly 19,500 square meter industrial zoned site, comprising the converted warehouse, with basement and ground floor, plus a separate four story building with its own basement, matching this Rivoli location. Neither Noovle nor third party directories checked this session disclose specific power capacity in megawatts, technical floor area, or Tier certification for this particular building, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. Noovle S.p.A. is the cloud computing subsidiary of Italian telecom TIM, operating within the TIM Enterprise division, and serves as Google Clouds infrastructure partner in Italy, building and operating the data centers underlying Google Clouds Milan and Turin regions. TIMs own technical newsletter describes the wider Noovle network, of which this Rivoli site is one part, as spanning 16 data centers across Italy totaling about 40,000 square meters, 60,000 servers, and 40 megawatts of total IT electrical power, an aggregate figure across all Noovle sites rather than this building specifically. Rivoli itself is a town on Turins western outskirts historically known for industrial and manufacturing activity, and the choice of an industrial warehouse conversion for this data center, rather than new construction on greenfield land, reflects a broader pattern across Noovles Turin area buildout in which the company has repurposed existing industrial real estate across several of its sites, including this Rivoli location alongside its separate Cebrosa and Moncalieri facilities tracked as their own rows elsewhere in this registry.
